seoTitle: It's Always Sunny Test: Which Character Are You? (12 Questions)
metaDescription: Take the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia test: 12 everyday questions reveal whether you're Charlie, Dennis, Mac, Dee, Frank, the Waitress, Cricket or Artemis — with your full character breakdown.
intro: Are you the wild card, the golden god, or the one funding every bad idea? Answer 12 everyday questions about schemes, friends and bad decisions, and find out which It's Always Sunny character you are.

characters.name: Charlie Kelly
characters.title: The Wild Card
characters.summary: Sweet, chaotic and full of ideas nobody else would ever have. You're a lot smarter than you look, in very specific ways.
description: Like Charlie, you do the jobs nobody else will. He's Paddy's Pub's janitor, and the gang calls the worst tasks 'Charlie work'.
You're secretly talented. Charlie can barely read, but he plays piano, sings and even wrote his own musical, The Nightman Cometh.
You're loyal to a fault. Charlie has loved the Waitress for years, no matter how many times she turns him down.
characters.flaw: You commit to a terrible plan completely, and nobody can talk you out of it.
characters.signature: A rat stick, a notebook of song ideas and a bed you share with Frank.
characters.clashReason: they'd come up with a plan so strange you couldn't even argue with it

characters.name: Dennis Reynolds
characters.title: The Golden God
characters.summary: Vain, clever and very sure of himself. You think you're the smartest person in the room, and you'd like everyone to admit it.
description: Like Dennis, you think you're above all this. He went to the University of Pennsylvania, and he never lets the gang forget it.
You've always got a system. Dennis has a step-by-step method for winning people over, which he calls the D.E.N.N.I.S. System.
You don't take criticism well. Dennis likes to think he's the voice of reason, but he snaps the moment anyone makes him feel insecure.
characters.flaw: One small insult and the whole calm, superior act falls apart.
characters.signature: A perfect hairline, a mirror nearby and a five-step plan for everything.
characters.clashReason: they'd explain, very slowly, why you're wrong about everything

characters.name: Mac
characters.title: The Wannabe Tough Guy
characters.summary: Proud, loyal and desperate to look like a badass. You want respect, and you'd really like everyone to see your moves.
description: Like Mac, you want people to think you're tough. He's Paddy's 'bouncer', and he's always bragging about his martial arts skills.
You care what people think more than you'd admit. Mac has spent his whole life trying to impress his dad, Luther.
You get there in the end. It takes him years, but Mac finally comes out and gets comfortable being himself.
characters.flaw: You talk a much bigger game than you can actually play.
characters.signature: Cut-off sleeves, a karate stance and a lot of talk about being a badass.
characters.clashReason: they'd show off in front of you, then insist they meant to fall over

characters.name: Dee Reynolds
characters.title: The Aspiring Star
characters.summary: Ambitious, dramatic and tougher than anyone gives you credit for. You were born for the spotlight, even if the spotlight disagrees.
description: Like Dee, you dream big. She's a bartender at Paddy's who desperately wants to be an actress or a comedian.
You're your own worst enemy on stage. Dee has terrible stage fright, which doesn't help her acting career.
You can take a lot. The gang calls Dee a 'bird' and makes fun of her constantly, and she keeps coming back for more.
characters.flaw: You want the attention so badly that you'll take any kind you can get.
characters.signature: A headshot nobody asked for, an audition outfit and a lot of comebacks.
characters.clashReason: they'd turn your big moment into their big moment

characters.name: Frank Reynolds
characters.title: The Rich Lunatic
characters.summary: Rich, gross and up for absolutely anything. You've got the money to fund any bad idea, and you usually do.
description: Like Frank, you love a scheme. He bought most of Paddy's Pub, and he pays for most of the gang's terrible plans.
You don't care how things look. Frank has plenty of money, but he chooses to live in a filthy apartment with Charlie.
You've given up on being respectable. Frank divorced his wife, Barbara, and moved in with Charlie to relive his misspent youth, however disgusting it gets.
characters.flaw: You think anything is fine as long as you can pay your way out of it.
characters.signature: A wad of cash, a shady business deal and a toe knife.
characters.clashReason: they'd fund your idea, then make it much, much worse

characters.name: The Waitress
characters.title: The Hopeless Romantic
characters.summary: Hard-working, bitter and trying to keep it all together. You keep falling for exactly the wrong person.
description: Like the Waitress, you know how to work hard. She waits tables at a coffee shop near Paddy's Pub.
You fall for the wrong people. She's had a crush on Dennis for years, even though he treats her terribly.
You're trying to get your life on track. She's a recovering alcoholic, and she even becomes Charlie's sponsor. Nobody ever learns her name.
characters.flaw: You keep giving second chances to people who've earned none.
characters.signature: A coffee pot, a sigh and a crush you know is a terrible idea.
characters.clashReason: they'd be sick of your nonsense before you'd even said hello

characters.name: Rickety Cricket
characters.title: The Survivor
characters.summary: Long-suffering, unlucky and impossible to get rid of. Life keeps knocking you down, and you keep getting back up.
description: Like Cricket, you used to have it all together. Matthew Mara was a priest before he got caught up with the gang.
You've had terrible luck. After the gang got involved in his life, Cricket lost his job and his home, and he's been in some truly awful situations.
You hold a grudge, but you keep turning up anyway. Cricket hates the gang for what they did to him, and he still keeps crossing paths with them.
characters.flaw: You keep trusting the people who've hurt you before.
characters.signature: A battered face, a long list of grudges and an old priest's collar.
characters.clashReason: they'd remind you of every bad thing you've ever done to them

characters.name: Artemis
characters.title: The Free Spirit
characters.summary: Eccentric, fearless and totally shameless. You take your art very seriously, and you never apologise for being yourself.
description: Like Artemis, you take your craft seriously. She's Dee's friend from acting class, and she gives every scene everything she's got.
You've got your own way of doing things. Artemis has some very strange habits, and she isn't embarrassed by any of them.
You're the closest thing to a normal friend the gang has. Artemis gets dragged into their schemes, and she somehow always goes along with it.
characters.flaw: You overshare, and then you overshare some more.
characters.signature: A dramatic scarf, an acting exercise and absolutely no shame.
characters.clashReason: they'd tell you something about themselves you could never unhear

questions.text: Your boss asks for a volunteer to clean up a disgusting mess. You...

options.text: Do it. Someone has to, and you don't mind getting your hands dirty
Point out that this is clearly beneath you
Volunteer someone else before anyone can volunteer you
Do it, and keep anything valuable you find

questions.text: Someone leaves a harsh review of something you made. You...

options.text: Write a long reply explaining why they're wrong, then another one
Decide they're jealous. Your work speaks for itself
Take it as a good sign. Real art always upsets someone
Shrug. You've had much worse days than this
The gym, then the bar, so everyone can see how hard you trained
Staying in with something weird to eat and a half-finished craft project
Something experimental that most people would find too strange
A big night out that you don't remember the end of

questions.text: Your friends come up with a plan to make some quick cash. You...

options.text: Put the money in, as long as you get a cut of everything
Put yourself in charge. You're the only one with a brain
Insist on a part where you get to perform
Say no. These things always end with someone getting hurt

questions.text: Someone you like hasn't noticed you exist. You...

options.text: Keep showing up wherever they are, just in case
Keep hoping, even though you know they're bad news
Assume it's never going to happen. It never does
Just tell them. Directly. Possibly too directly

questions.text: You're asked to stand up and say a few words at a party. You...

options.text: Freeze, then say something you'll replay in your head for years
Turn it into a full performance, with a song
Show everyone a few of your moves while you've got their attention
Keep it short. The last thing you need is people looking at you

questions.text: You find a wallet on the street. You...

options.text: Keep the cash, and get rid of the wallet
Hand it in, then tell everyone what a good person you are
Give it back, and quietly hope there's a reward
Hand it straight in. It's not worth the guilt

questions.text: A friend asks what you honestly think of their new haircut. It's bad. You...

options.text: Tell them it's awful, and that you're worried about them as a person
Tell them the truth, then offer to cut it again yourself
Laugh, then go and tell everyone else
Tell them it looks great. You'd hate to upset them

questions.text: You make a mistake at work, and someone else gets the blame. You...

options.text: Let them take it, and offer to buy them a drink later
Join in blaming them. Loudly
Feel awful, and quietly try to make it up to them
Deny everything. You'd never make a mistake like that

questions.text: You sign up for an evening class. On the first night, you...

options.text: Sit at the front and treat it like the most important thing in the world
Get nervous, then try way too hard to be the best
Work out who in the room you could date
Leave at the break. You knew you'd hate it

questions.text: You own a bar with your friends, and it never has any customers. You...

options.text: Come up with a big, insane plan to fix it by Friday
Remind everyone whose money is keeping the place open
Turn it into a stage and put on a show
Make yourself head of security and wait for trouble

questions.text: Your group of friends are, honestly, terrible people, and they've let you down again. You...

options.text: Keep hanging around. They're the only friends you've got
Swear you'll get them back for it, one day
Tell yourself this is the last time. Again
Go along with whatever they're doing next. Why fight it?
